L2_blanket_auto.property: unattended operation must not depend on unrestricted tool approval
evidence_independent: installed CLI help text for --auto reads: 'auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)'
the dispatcher only appends --auto when cfg.auto_approve is truthy; the default path does not add it
the worker reports the positive E2E required --auto and that without it OpenCode rejected the fixture write with 'external_directory'
L2_blanket_auto.reviewer_limitation: the live escalation test (agent performing an out-of-terrain write once --auto is on) could NOT be executed here because the CLI cannot create its log file under the review sandbox. The worker's live observation is credible and CLI-corroborated but not reviewer-reproduced.
L2_blanket_auto.what_auto_actually_grants: auto-approval of every permission not explicitly denied -- i.e. the runtime stops asking the human. Combined with zero OS containment (L1), a commissioned agent under --auto is not bounded by the dispatcher at all: the dispatcher's terrain gate is an AFTER-THE-FACT git-diff check, not a preventive control.
L2_blanket_auto.minimum_repair: replace blanket --auto with a scoped permission profile covering exactly the task terrain, and prove an out-of-terrain write is DENIED by the runtime rather than merely detected afterwards

L1_no_containment.property: the dispatcher must enforce, not merely assert, the worker's bounds
evidence: source review of the 766-line dispatcher: enforcement is entirely advisory state/Git law -- validateTask, terrainGate, publicationGate, Store, deliverReturn
no chroot/container/seccomp/namespace/rlimit/setuid/user separation anywhere in the module
workers are spawned with plain child_process.spawn and inherit the reviewer's user identity and filesystem access
distinct worktrees and distinct pids are distinctness, not isolation -- the worker correctly did NOT claim containment
L1_no_containment.consequence: the terrain gate constrains what may be PUBLISHED, not what may be WRITTEN. A worker can write anywhere the user can; the dispatcher detects out-of-terrain tracked changes only at publication time, and only if they are committed inside the candidate diff.
L1_no_containment.minimum_repair: an OS-level or process-level isolation mechanism (container, sandbox-exec profile, separate unprivileged user with filesystem ACLs) -- or an explicit decision that unattended operation is out of scope

combined_assessment: L1 + L2 together mean an unattended commissioned agent runs with blanket tool approval and no runtime containment. Neither the terrain gate nor the identity gates prevent an action; they only adjudicate its artifacts. This is the decisive reason unattended operation is not qualified.
